title: Invariant subspaces of algebraic l-adic representations descend continuously
statement: Let l be prime, K an algebraic closure of Q_l, G a profinite group, and rho an l-adic representation on a K-vector space V in the sense of [def-pod-l-adic-representations]. If U is a K-linear subspace with an action tau satisfying tau(g)(v)=rho(g)(v) in V for all g and v in U, then tau is l-adic in the same sense: it has a finite-dimensional continuous model over a finite subextension of K, with canonical scalar-extension comparison.

source.place: First six sentences; invariant-subspace descent in step 2 of lem-zl-common-irreducibility-detecting-cover, also Deligne Weil II (1.1.6).

proof.text: Choose a continuous finite coefficient model W over E from IsLAdic and an E-basis c of W. Its scalar extension, followed by the canonical comparison, is a K-basis a of the ambient representation. In this basis the ambient action matrices are scalar extensions of continuous E-valued matrices B(g).

Choose a K-basis b of the invariant subspace U and a K-linear projection p onto U. Let J and P be the matrices of inclusion U to V and projection V to U in b and a. Since p restricts to the identity on U and U is invariant, the restricted action has matrix P B(g) J over K. This includes the zero subspace and zero-dimensional ambient model.

Adjoin to E all finitely many entries of P and J. They are algebraic over Q_l, so their compositum L with E is a finite extension of Q_l inside K. The displayed formula gives matrices over L. Their multiplication and inverse identities follow by the injectivity of L to K from those of the given restricted action. The inclusion E to L is Q_l-linear between finite-dimensional normed vector spaces, hence continuous for the spectral norms. Therefore the matrix formula has continuous entries and gives a jointly continuous action on the coordinate L-vector space.

Map the coordinate L-vector space into U by the basis b and take its image W_L as an actual submodule. Linear independence of b makes this map an isomorphism onto W_L, and equivariance transports the constructed continuous action to W_L. The finite-basis base-change theorem identifies K tensor_L W_L with U by the canonical pure-tensor map. These data give exactly IsLAdic of the restricted action.

proof_origin.place: Invariant-subspace argument in the first six sentences; coordinate projection version of the finite-coordinate descent argument.

theorem isLAdic_subrepresentation
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra ℚ_[l] K]
    [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] K] (G : ProfiniteGrp.{v})
    (V : Type w) [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V]
    (ρ : G →* (V ≃ₗ[K] V)) (hρ : IsLAdic l K G V ρ)
    (U : Submodule K V) (τ : G →* (U ≃ₗ[K] U))
    (hτ : ∀ (g : G) (v : U), (τ g v : V) = ρ g (v : V)) :
    IsLAdic l K G U τ
